items.title: Kerala is now officially ‘Keralam’ as Union govt notifies name change
items.summary: Kerala is officially ‘Keralam’ with effect from August 25 after the Union Home Ministry notified the new name of the southern state and brought the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026 into force. The notification comes just ahead of Onam, which is the traditional harvest festival of Kerala and one of the state’s most widely celebrated festivals. In a gazette notification issued on Tuesday, August 25, the Home Ministry said, “In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (2) of Section 1 of the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, the Central government hereby appoints the 25th day of August, 2026, as the date on which the provisions of the said Act shall come into force.” President Droupadi Murmu had earlier this month given her assent to the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, turning it into law. The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on August 11, followed by the Rajya Sabha on August 12. Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai said during the Rajya Sabha debate that the Kerala Assembly had passed a resolution in 2024 urging the Union government to change the state’s name to Keralam. “The Bill provides that the State of Kerala will be known as the State of Keralam, and he

CMS INDUSLAW advised Freehand on this fundraise. The transaction team consisted of Winnie Shekhar (Partner), Shantanu Singh (Partner) and Ravishankar M (Senior Associate). Freehand Freehand develops autonomous AI agents that manage enterprise supply-chain spend, including contract enforcement, supplier management, invoice processing, payment workflows and spend reconciliation. Its platform is deployed by leading global enterprises including Meta, Unilever, Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, Dunkin' and Cardinal Health. The fresh capital will support the expansion of its AI platform and enterprise deployments. items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Tamil Nadu government will explore using land acquired for the now-scrapped Parandur greenfield airport project for alternative industrial projects, Industries Minister S Keerthana told the Assembly on Tuesday, August 25. Speaking during the debate on the Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce, Keerthana said the government would explore industrial projects that do not affect the environment or the livelihoods of people in the region. Such projects would help create employment opportunities and promote economic growth in Parandur, she said. Her statement came a day after Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced in the Assembly that the proposed Parandur airport project would be scrapped. Keerthana said the acquired land could be used for other public purposes under Clause 99 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which permits a change in land-use purpose in case of unforeseen circumstances. items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Telangana police have arrested Vinod Kumar in connection with the death of 32-year-old Ankathi Manasa, whose body was found stuffed in the boot of a car in Hanamkonda’s Elkathurthi mandal. Her father, Ankathi Rajesham was also arrested. Ankathi Manasa’s body was discovered after locals noticed a foul smell coming from a car parked near the agricultural market checkpost on August 21. The police, who were alerted by the village secretary, found the body wrapped in a blanket inside the vehicle. An Aadhaar card recovered from the car helped establish the woman’s identity. Yadelli Vinod Kumar (34) was taken into custody on August 24 by a special police team from the outskirts of Elkathurthi. Rajesham was subsequently arrested on Monday night. According to police, Manasa and Vinod were childhood friends and were in a romantic relationship. Vinod also knew Manasa’s family well. Justice V Lakshminarayanan issued the warning while hearing the election petitions concerning Vijay’s victories from the Perambur and Tiruchirappalli East constituencies and Aadhav Arjuna’s victory from Villivakkam. According to LiveLaw , Justice Lakshminarayanan orally remarked, “I'm not bothered about the personalities. You people say that election cases are not being decided. But then you are asking time. Election petitions are to be disposed of within 6 months.” The judge stressed that the court was working within the statutory six-month period for disposing of election petitions and therefore could not permit prolonged adjournments. items.title: CPI hits out at Pinarayi over Deputy Leader of Opposition row
items.summary: The CPI has stepped up its criticism of CPI(M) leader and Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan over his reported decision to nominate a CPI(M) leader as Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the Kerala Assembly. CPI said the move violates coalition norms and the principles of Left politics. In an article published in the CPI mouthpiece Janayugam , party assistant secretary Sathyan Mokeri said the decision cannot be taken unilaterally by the Leader of the Opposition as discussions between the CPI and CPI(M) were still underway. “The statement made by the Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on the issue of the Deputy Leader of the Opposition can only be viewed as a complete violation of coalition etiquette and as an absence of the political ethics that must be upheld in coalition politics,” Mokeri wrote. The CPI had proposed the creation of the Deputy Leader of the Opposition post following the LDF's defeat in the Assembly elections, with the aim of strengthening the coalition's collective functioning, he said. items.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, on Tuesday, August 25, said he does not support the planned Madison Square Garden event where Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat is scheduled to address members of the Indian diaspora, but said he was unsure whether the city had the authority to cancel a private event. Bhagwat is scheduled to address around 5,000 people at Madison Square Garden on Saturday, August 29, as part of the RSS’s centenary-year global outreach programme. He arrived in the United States on Tuesday and is also expected to participate in the Universal Oneness programme during his stay in New York. Mamdani said at a news conference, “I don't support the rally, but I don't know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event.” His remarks came in response to questions about the RSS, the planned Madison Square Garden event and protests against Bhagwat’s appearance. Mamdani, who is the first Indian-American mayor in New York City’s history, also referred to his family background while explaining his opposition to the event.
